children: Korean subsidiary has signed a 10-project deal with South Korea’s Kakao Entertainment to collaborate on projects that leverage the success of K-Pop and Disney’s intellectual property.
The two companies will collaborate on the creation of a tentatively named K-Culture Fund and “elevate the paradigm of the K-IP ecosystem to the next level.”

“Through this partnership, we look forward to bringing K-pop artists and music together with Disney’s stories—which have been loved around the world for generations—and expanding them into new worlds," Kakao said in a press release.
By capitalizing on the massive popularity of the genre, Disney+

has accumulated a substantial library of K-pop content that includes concert footage, documentaries, and reality shows. The deal with Kakao intends to expand on Disney’s catalog as well as the massive cultural K-pop phenomenon through music, content, commerce, and performances.

K-pop has evolved over the last 15 years from vocal acts and viral hits to a multi-billion dollar Korean juggernaut, driving billions of dollars to the South Korean economy through its valuable intellectual property, concerts, movies, and TV shows.
